summary.title: Powerups (LearnOpenGL: 2D Breakout)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to model, spawn, activate, time out and render falling powerup blocks in a C++ OpenGL Breakout clone.
takeaways: Model a powerup as a GameObject subclass with a type string, duration, and activated flag, and store active powerups in a vector.
Spawn a powerup with a small random chance (rand() % chance == 0) when a non-solid brick is destroyed, using different odds for positive and negative powerups.
Activate a powerup on paddle collision by changing game state (ball velocity, paddle size, ball/paddle flags, postprocessing effects).
Update powerups each frame by moving them downward and counting down their duration, reverting effects only when no other powerup of the same type remains active.
Sticky and pass-through effects are stored as ball properties and checked in collision logic.
summary.summary: The page extends the Breakout tutorial with powerups: falling blocks spawned from destroyed bricks with a random chance, which the player collects with the paddle to gain effects. It defines four positive powerups (speed, sticky, pass-through, pad-size-increase) and two negative ones (confuse, chaos), each with a C++ code example for spawning, activation, collision handling, timed deactivation, and rendering. Effects are tracked through ball and paddle properties and postprocessing flags, and a helper prevents an effect from ending while another powerup of the same type is still active.
